desc: Implement a Fenwick Tree (BIT) that supports range updates and point queries. Specifically, use the standard technique: to add $v$ to $[l, r]$, update BIT at $l$ with $+v$ and at $r+1$ with $-v$. Point query at $i$ returns the prefix sum up to $i$.
Initialize the BIT to represent $h(X) = X$. Since the BIT will store the difference $h(X) - X$, initialize it with zeros. The actual value $h(X)$ is computed as $X + \text{BIT.query}(X)$.
For each contest $(L_i, R_i)$, binary search for the smallest $A_i \in [1, M]$ such that $h(A_i) \ge L_i$. Use the monotonicity of $h$.
For each contest $(L_i, R_i)$, binary search for the largest $B_i \in [1, M]$ such that $h(B_i) \le R_i$.
If $A_i \le B_i$, perform a range add of +1 on the interval $[A_i, B_i]$ in the BIT.
After processing all $N$ contests, answer each query $X$ by computing $X + \text{BIT.query}(X)$ and printing the result.
